before.label: Jacob
before.description: Jacob is the younger twin born to Isaac and Rebekah, described as a quiet man living in tents. Esau sells his birthright to him in the account of the lentil stew.

after.label: Jacob (Israel)
after.description: Jacob, also named Israel, is Isaac and Rebekah’s son and the father of the twelve sons listed in Genesis 35. He marries Leah and Rachel, returns from Laban’s household, and reconciles with Esau.

disposition.reason: Israel renaming is explicit35:10; expanded marriage, family, return and reconciliation summary is source-supported. Collective Israel/poetic Jacob uses remain excluded by scoped aliases.

before.label: Laban
before.description: Laban is Rebekah’s brother, who welcomes Abraham’s servant and participates in the discussion of her departure and marriage. This pilot stops before Laban’s later stories.

after.label: Laban
after.description: Laban is Bethuel’s son, Rebekah’s brother, and Leah and Rachel’s father. Jacob serves in his household and later leaves with his family; the two men conclude an agreement after Laban overtakes him.

disposition.reason: Expanded description correctly uses Bethuel as Laban’s father28:5, Rebekah as sister24:29, Leah/Rachel as daughters29:16, and agreement31:44,53. This is passage expansion, not changed identity.
